sections.heading: When to buy mold shells vs complete blow molds
list: Choose shells when the line runs several bottle sizes, for example 330ml, 500ml, 550ml and 1.5L water bottles, and changes format often.
Choose shells when new bottle designs are introduced regularly, because each design then needs only inserts and a base mold.
Choose complete molds when a line runs one bottle for a long time and changeover speed is not a priority.
Check what the machine supports: some blow molding machines are designed for shell-type quick-change molds, others for complete molds only.

LIHE supplies split-type quick-change blow molds for two-step machines such as SIDEL, KRONES, SIG/KHS, TECH-LONG and NEWAMSTAR, and mold shells made from customers' existing parts or drawings for SIDEL, KRONES, KHS and other machines.
If existing shells are in good condition, a new format may only need new inserts; if the shells are worn, replace them first.

sections.heading: Format changeover steps with a shell-type blow mold
steps: Prepare the new cavity inserts, base molds and any blowing pins or conversion parts for the new bottle before stopping the line.
Stop the machine, follow the lockout procedure, vent blowing air and drain or isolate the mold cooling circuit.
Unbolt and remove the old cavity inserts from the shells, leaving the shells mounted in the carrier.
Clean the shell contact surfaces and locating features, and inspect the seals at the water transfer points.
Mount the new inserts on the locating features and tighten the fasteners to the specified torque.
Change the base mold, reconnect cooling, and pressure-check every station for leaks.
Load the process settings for the new bottle, run a trial and inspect parting line, base center and bottle dimensions from each station.

sections.heading: Mold shell inspection, wear and replacement
list: Inspect locating faces and pins of the shell at each format change; worn locators allow inserts to shift and create parting line steps.
Look for corrosion or scale in cooling channels and on contact faces, and check water quality if deposits return quickly.
Check threads of fastening holes; damaged threads prevent correct clamping of inserts.
LIHE's stated lead time for replacement parts is 4 weeks, so order replacement shells before worn ones affect production.
LIHE has an in-house Zeiss CMM lab and supplies inspection reports on request, which helps verify that new shells match existing inserts.

faq.question: What is the difference between a mold shell and a cavity insert?
faq.answer: The mold shell is the permanent holder that mounts in the machine and connects to the cooling circuit. The cavity insert carries the bottle shape and is exchanged when the bottle format changes.

faq.question: Does a shell system affect bottle cooling?
faq.answer: Heat passes from the insert through the shell contact surface into the cooling water, so this interface must be clean and flat and the water seals intact. With good contact and correct channel layout, the shell system supports even mold temperature.

faq.question: Can I use my existing shells for a new bottle design?
faq.answer: Often yes, if the new bottle fits the insert envelope of the existing shells and the shells are not worn. Send the shell drawing or a sample with the new bottle drawing to confirm.

faq.question: Are shell systems suitable for hot fill bottles?
faq.answer: Hot fill bottles, filled at about 85–95°C, need heat-set molds with specific temperature control. State the fill type at the start so the shell and insert design match the application.

faq.question: What do I need to send to order mold shells?
faq.answer: Send the machine make and model, existing shells or their drawings, the cooling connection layout and the bottle drawing. LIHE makes mold shells from customers' existing parts or drawings.

product-39.heading: Blow mold clamping base alignment: parting line quality, remounting and aluminum vs steel
product-39.intro: A clamping base is a machined base plate that connects the blow mold halves and the base mold to the mold carrier of a stretch blow molding machine and fixes their position. Because every mold change starts and ends at the clamping base, its mounting faces and locating features decide whether the two bottle halves meet exactly at the parting line. This guide explains what misalignment does to bottles, how to inspect and remount a clamping base, and how aluminum and steel bases compare in general terms.

sections.heading: What clamping base misalignment causes in PET blow molds
paragraphs: When the clamping base, shells or base mold do not sit in their intended position, the mold halves no longer close on a common plane. The result is visible on the bottle long before the mold is damaged.
list: Parting line mismatch: a step between the two bottle halves that can be felt with a fingernail and is visible on labels and transparent bottles.
Flash or a raised seam: material pushed into a gap between halves that do not close fully under blowing pressure.
Base mismatch: an off-center or stepped base when the base mold is not concentric with the side halves.
Dimensional variation: bottle diameter, ovality or height that differs between stations of the same machine.
Accelerated wear: uneven contact concentrates load on part of the parting face, which wears shells and inserts faster.
Cooling problems: shifted mounting can strain water connections and cause leaks or reduced flow in one mold half.

Heat-set (hot fill) molds run with heated walls for bottles filled at about 85–95°C, and standard PET deforms above about 60°C, so a clamping base for a heat-set mold must hold alignment while the mold is hot.

sections.heading: Where alignment comes from: mounting faces, locating features and fasteners
list: Mounting faces: flat, clean contact surfaces between the carrier, the clamping base and the shell or mold half. Dents, burrs or dried deposits tilt the mold.
Locating features: dowel pins, keys, bushings or locating shoulders that set the position of each part. Worn pins and enlarged holes allow movement after each mold change.
Fasteners: bolts tightened to the machine maker's specified torque in the specified order. Uneven tightening can pull a half out of position.
Base mold guidance: the base mold must be centered relative to the side halves at the closed position; its guide and lift mechanism also affect the base parting line.
Temperature: heated or cooled molds expand and contract, so alignment should be checked at operating temperature as well as cold.

sections.heading: Inspection steps before remounting a clamping base
steps: Stop the machine, follow the lockout procedure, release blowing air and drain the cooling circuit of the mold station.
Remove the mold halves and base mold and clean all mounting faces on the carrier and clamping base with a non-abrasive method.
Inspect mounting faces for dents, burrs, corrosion and deposits; remove raised burrs carefully without changing the face geometry.
Check dowel pins, keys and locating bores for wear, looseness and enlarged diameters, and replace worn locating parts.
Check flatness of the clamping base on a surface plate or with a straightedge and feeler gauges, and compare with the drawing.
Inspect water connections and seals, and replace seals that are flattened or cracked.
Record the findings per station so that recurring problems on one position can be traced.

sections.heading: Remounting steps for clean parting lines
steps: Mount the clamping base on its locating features first, then tighten the fasteners to the specified torque in a cross pattern.
Mount the mold halves on the clamping base, engaging the locating pins before any bolt is tightened.
Close the mold slowly in setup mode and check that both halves meet evenly; a contact check with marking compound shows gaps on the parting faces.
Check centering and height of the base mold in the closed position.
Connect cooling water, pressure the circuit and check every connection for leaks before heating or blowing.
Run a short trial, then inspect the parting line, base center and key dimensions of bottles from each station.
Keep the first bottles from each station as reference samples for the next mold change.

sections.heading: Clamping base replacement and dimensional verification
list: Replace a clamping base when its locating bores or mounting faces are worn beyond what new pins or bushings can correct.
LIHE makes clamping bases from customers' existing parts or drawings for SIDEL, KRONES, KHS and other blow molding machines.
Water connections and channels are matched to the mold's cooling circuit, so send the existing cooling layout with the order.
LIHE has an in-house Zeiss CMM lab, and inspection reports are supplied on request.
LIHE's stated lead time for replacement parts is 4 weeks; plan replacements together with scheduled mold changes.
For hot fill bottles, where the mold runs at a different temperature than for cold fill (filling at about 85–95°C), state the fill type so the base and its cooling connections suit the application.

faq.question: Why does my bottle show a step at the parting line?
faq.answer: A step usually means the two mold halves are offset. Common causes are dirt or burrs on mounting faces, worn dowel pins or bushings, uneven bolt tightening, or a worn clamping base. Check the station that produces the step first.

faq.question: Is flash at the parting line always caused by the clamping base?
faq.answer: No. Flash can also come from worn parting faces on the mold halves, insufficient clamping or locking force, or damage to the mold edges. If the mold halves are in good condition and flash remains, check the clamping base mounting and locating features.

faq.question: Should I choose an aluminum or a steel clamping base?
faq.answer: Follow the machine design. Aluminum is lighter and conducts heat well; steel is stiffer and more wear resistant. LIHE machines clamping bases from high-strength aluminum alloy or steel according to machine requirements.

faq.question: How often should clamping base alignment be checked?
faq.answer: Check it at every mold change, after any collision or blow-out, and whenever parting line or base defects appear in one station. Logging the results per station shows when wear starts.

faq.question: What information is needed to order a replacement clamping base?
faq.answer: Send the machine make and model, the existing part or its drawing, the cooling connection layout and the bottle drawing. LIHE makes clamping bases from customers' existing parts or drawings.

product-40.heading: Format change parts for PET bottle lines: star wheels, guides and neck grippers for bottle, neck finish and preform changes
product-40.intro: A format change part is a bottle- or preform-specific part of a blowing or bottle handling line, such as a star wheel, transfer guide or neck gripper, that is exchanged when the line switches to a different bottle, neck finish or preform. They decide whether preforms and bottles move through the line without jams, scratches or falls. This guide explains which parts change for each type of format change, what measurement data a supplier needs, and how to run the changeover in a controlled order.

sections.heading: What changes with a new bottle, neck finish or preform
paragraphs: Not every format change needs a full set of new parts. The parts affected depend on which dimension changes: the bottle body, the neck finish or the preform.
list: New bottle shape or capacity, for example from 500ml to 1.5L: star wheel pockets, transfer and outfeed guides, and other parts that touch the bottle body.
New neck finish, for example from PCO 1810 to PCO 1881 or to a 38mm finish: neck grippers, neck guides and any part that holds the preform or bottle by the support ring or neck.
New preform length or weight with the same neck: infeed rails and preform handling parts may need checking, and the blow mold, stretch rod and heating settings must suit the new preform.
Same bottle on a different blowing machine: conversion parts that let one blow mold run on different blowing equipment.
Lightweight bottles: thinner walls and lighter necks can change how bottles behave in grippers and guides, so contact parts should be checked even if nominal dimensions stay similar.

sections.heading: Measurement data to send for conversion parts
paragraphs: Accurate input data is the main factor in whether new parts fit the first time. Send as much of the following as possible.
list: Machine make, model and serial number for every machine the parts must fit, for example SIDEL, KRONES or KHS equipment.
Bottle drawing with body diameter, height, shoulder and base geometry, and the position of label panels.
Neck finish drawing with thread diameter, support ring diameter and thickness, and the distance between support ring and neck top.
Preform drawing with length, neck finish and weight.
Existing parts or their drawings; LIHE makes conversion parts from customers' existing parts or drawings.
Photos of the current parts installed, showing identification marks and fixing points.
Fill type (cold fill, hot fill at about 85–95°C, or aseptic), because hot-filled bottles can be softer during handling.

sections.heading: Changeover steps for star wheels, guides and neck grippers
steps: Prepare the complete format kit in advance, check it against the parts list and mark each part with its position on the line.
Run out the old format, stop the line and follow the lockout procedure for every machine that will be changed.
Remove old star wheels, guides and neck grippers in a fixed order and store them as a kit for the next changeover.
Install the new parts on their locating features and fasten them without forcing; parts that do not fit freely should be checked, not hammered.
Set adjustable guides to the new bottle or neck dimensions using a sample bottle or preform as a gauge.
Turn the line by hand or at slow speed and watch every transfer point for contact, scratches or misalignment.
Run production samples, check for neck damage, scuffing and falls, then increase to normal speed and record the settings for the next changeover.

sections.heading: Reducing format change time on a PET bottle line
list: Single-minute exchange of die (SMED) methods aim to complete changeovers in under 10 minutes by moving as much work as possible to the time before the line stops.
Store each format as a complete, labelled kit so nothing is searched for during the stop.
Use parts with fixed locating features instead of parts that must be adjusted by eye.
Order conversion parts with the new blow mold as one complete format change package, so the mold, blowing parts and handling parts are made to the same drawings.
Plan lead times: LIHE's stated lead time for replacement parts is 4 weeks; plan new formats so that molds and change parts arrive together.

sections.heading: Common fitting problems after a format change
list: Bottles falling at a transfer point: pocket or guide dimensions do not match the bottle, or timing between star wheels is off.
Scuffing on the bottle body: guides set too tight or contact surfaces worn.
Neck finish marks or damaged support rings: neck grippers do not match the new neck finish dimensions.
Jams at the infeed: preform length or neck dimensions differ from what the infeed rails were made for.
Parts that fit one machine but not another of the same type: machine versions differ, so always send the model and serial number.

faq.question: Which parts must change when only the neck finish changes?
faq.answer: Usually the neck grippers, neck guides and blowing pins, because they touch the neck or support ring. Star wheels that handle the bottle body may stay the same if the bottle body is unchanged.

faq.question: Can one blow mold run on different blowing machines?
faq.answer: Yes, with conversion parts that adapt the mold mounting and handling to each machine. LIHE supplies conversion parts for running one blow mold on different blowing machines.

faq.question: What is the most common cause of conversion parts not fitting?
faq.answer: Incomplete input data, especially a missing machine model or serial number, or a bottle drawing that does not match the final bottle. Sending existing parts or their drawings reduces this risk.

faq.question: Should conversion parts be ordered with the blow mold?
faq.answer: It is usually better, because the mold, blowing parts and handling parts are then made to the same bottle and neck drawings. LIHE supplies conversion parts with the new blow mold as a complete format change package.

faq.question: How long does it take to get conversion parts?
faq.answer: LIHE's stated lead time for replacement parts is 4 weeks. Plan new formats so that conversion parts and molds are ready before the planned launch date.

product-42.heading: Planning a bottle format change: which blow molding machine accessories and conversion parts you need
product-42.intro: A blow molding accessories kit is a set of machine-side parts, such as blowing pins, stretch rods, clamping bases, mold shells and conversion parts, that lets a blow molder run a new neck finish, bottle shape or capacity, or a mold from another machine. This guide shows which parts each type of change usually requires, and gives a checklist and a step-by-step plan so the parts arrive together with the blow mold and the launch is not held up by one missing item.

sections.heading: Why format changes stall on small parts
paragraphs: A new bottle is usually planned around the blow mold and the preform. The smaller parts that touch the preform and bottle on the way through the machine are often noticed only during installation, when the new mold is already on site. One wrong stretch rod or neck gripper can stop the start-up.
list: Parts that touch the neck: blowing pins (nozzles), neck grippers, transfer star wheels and guides at the neck support ring.
Parts that touch the body and base: mold shells, clamping bases and base mold holders.
Parts that move inside the preform: stretch rods, whose length and tip suit the bottle height and base.
Parts downstream of the blower: conveyor guides and star wheels sized for the new bottle diameter.
LIHE supplies blowing pins, stretch rods, clamping bases, mold shells and conversion parts such as star wheels, guides and neck grippers, and can deliver them together with the blow mold.

Replacement and conversion parts made from customers' existing parts or drawings are quoted with a 4-week lead time for replacement parts, and heat-set formats must respect the 60°C deformation point of standard PET.

sections.heading: Neck finish change: what to plan
list: Decide the new finish early, for example moving from PCO 1810 to the shorter PCO 1881 (both 28 mm), or to a short water neck such as 2925 or 2622.
The preform changes first; LIHE tooling conversion covers neck finish conversions of existing preform molds as well as new preform molds.
Blowing pins must seal on the new neck; their seal diameter and position follow the finish.
Neck grippers, star wheel pockets and guides that hold the neck support ring must match its new diameter and height.
Closure supply and capper chucks must be ready on the same date; a neck change without matching closures cannot start.

sections.heading: Shape, capacity and cross-machine changes: what to plan
list: Shape change with the same preform: the new blow mold or inserts are the main item; check the base mold and clamping base if the base design changes.
Capacity change: bottle height and diameter change, so stretch rods, base molds and downstream star wheels and guides usually change as well.
Hot fill products, filled at about 85–95°C, need heat-set blow molds; check that heated mold shells and connections exist on the machine before choosing this path.
Cross-machine conversion: to run one blow mold on another blower, the interface parts change, mainly mold shells or adapters, clamping bases, blowing pins and stretch rods.
Machine spare parts for SIDEL, KRONES, KHS and other blow molders can be made from your existing parts or drawings, which helps when original parts are slow to obtain.

sections.heading: Format change checklist before ordering
list: Old and new bottle drawings, with capacity, height, maximum diameter and base design.
Old and new preform drawings, with neck finish and preform length.
Blow molding machine brand, model, number of cavities and mold carrier type; for a conversion, both the source and the target machine.
Photos or drawings of the current blowing pins, stretch rods, clamping bases and neck grippers.
Filling type: still, carbonated or hot fill.
Downstream parts owned by other suppliers: filler, capper and labeler change parts.
Planned launch date and the date of the scheduled line stop for installation.

sections.heading: Timeline steps for a new product launch on an existing blow molder
steps: Define the change: new neck finish, new shape, new capacity, lightweighting or cross-machine conversion, or a combination.
Collect the checklist data and send it with the blow mold request so molds and accessories are reviewed together.
Agree the parts list against drawings: blow mold, preform or preform mold changes, and each accessory by part and quantity per cavity.
Order closures and filler, capper and labeler change parts from their suppliers in parallel.
Manufacture the blow mold and accessories; LIHE's engineering center uses CAD/CAM, 3D simulation and flow analysis, and inspection is done in LIHE's in-house Zeiss CMM lab.
Ship the blow mold and accessories as one delivery, packed and labeled by machine station.
Install during the planned line stop, blow sample bottles, check them and run the filler, capper and labeler with the new bottle before full production.

sections.heading: Common mistakes in format change projects
list: Ordering the blow mold before the preform is fixed, then finding that the stretch rod length or neck parts do not match.
Forgetting that one cavity count means one set of parts per cavity: blowing pins, stretch rods and clamping bases are needed for every station.
Assuming a mold from one machine brand fits another without conversion parts.
Leaving downstream conveyor star wheels and guides out of the plan for a new bottle diameter.
Not keeping spare blowing pins and stretch rods for the new format, so a single damaged part stops a station.

faq.question: Can accessories be ordered without a new blow mold?
faq.answer: Yes. Accessories and conversion parts can be ordered alone, for example to run an existing mold on another machine, to replace worn parts, or to adapt the line to a new preform. Machine spare parts can be made from your existing parts or drawings.

faq.question: What is needed to run my existing blow mold on a different blowing machine?
faq.answer: Usually conversion parts for the target machine: mold shells or adapters, clamping bases, blowing pins and stretch rods. Send the mold drawings and the source and target machine models so the interface can be checked.

faq.question: Does a neck finish change always require a new blow mold?
faq.answer: Not always. The body of the bottle may stay the same, but the preform changes and the neck-related parts, such as blowing pins, neck grippers and neck guides, must match the new finish. Whether the blow mold neck area needs changes is checked against the drawings.

faq.question: Which machines are the accessories made for?
faq.answer: Machine spare parts are made for SIDEL, KRONES, KHS and other blow molding machines from your existing parts or drawings. Blow molds and their accessories cover two-step SIDEL, KRONES, SIG/KHS, TECH-LONG and NEWAMSTAR machines and one-step SIPA, ASB and AOKI machines.

faq.question: Why deliver accessories together with the blow mold?
faq.answer: Because the start-up needs every part at the same time. One delivery, checked against one parts list, avoids waiting for a single missing stretch rod or neck gripper after the new mold has arrived.
